**Lunar Landing Site Navigator**

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an intelligent interactive application designed to help scientists and space mission planners identify the most suitable landing sites and times on the Moon’s South Pole.

We developed a system that analyzes and visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to potential landing locations. This allows users to understand lighting conditions, evaluate solar energy generation opportunities, and identify periods when direct communication with Earth is possible.

The project addresses one of the major challenges of lunar exploration: selecting landing locations that provide suitable conditions for lighting, energy generation, and communication. Through a user-friendly interface and interactive visualizations, users can easily compare different locations and time periods to make better-informed decisions.

The project's importance lies in supporting more efficient lunar mission planning, reducing operational challenges, and contributing to the future of human exploration on the Moon.
details:
Project Details – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive scientific decision-support application developed by Team SYNEXIS to help scientists and space mission planners identify and evaluate suitable landing sites and dates on the Moon’s South Pole.

How Does It Work?

The application analyzes astronomical and topographical data to evaluate different lunar landing scenarios. It uses NASA/JPL Horizons to calculate the positions and distances of the Sun and Earth relative to a selected landing location. It also uses NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) Digital Elevation Models (DEM) to analyze local terrain and horizon obstructions.

Based on these calculations, the system evaluates sunlight availability, potential solar energy generation opportunities, direct communication windows with Earth, and terrain-related mission conditions. Users can explore a specific location and date, compare up to four scenarios, and measure distances, surface profiles, and craters through interactive tools.

Benefits and Expected Impact

The project helps reduce the complexity of lunar mission planning by transforming complex scientific datasets into understandable, interactive information. It can support better-informed landing site selection, improve mission preparation, and help planners identify potential challenges related to lighting, energy, communication, and terrain.

Our long-term goal is to contribute to safer, more efficient, and sustainable human exploration of the Moon.

Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using:

  • TanStack Start, TanStack Router, and React 19: Application architecture and user interface.
  • TypeScript: Scientific calculations and application logic.
  • Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei: Interactive 3D lunar visualization.
  • Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn/ui: Interface design.
  • NASA/JPL Horizons API: Astronomical position and distance data.
  • NASA LOLA DEM: Lunar elevation and terrain data.
  • NASA LROC WAC: Lunar surface imagery.
  • Vite 8 and Nitro: Development and deployment infrastructure.
  • Vitest and ESLint: Testing and code quality.
  • NVIDIA Build API: Optional AI-powered explanations through our assistant, Selene.

What Makes It Innovative?

Unlike simple lunar maps or static landing site visualizations, our project combines astronomical calculations, real lunar elevation data, lighting analysis, and communication opportunities in one interactive decision-support platform. It also allows users to compare multiple landing scenarios rather than evaluating locations in isolation.

An important design principle is scientific reliability: calculations are based on documented sources and equations. If a data source is unavailable, the application clearly reports the limitation instead of displaying invented or fallback scientific values.

Factors Considered by Our Team

We considered several important factors, including solar illumination, terrain elevation, horizon obstructions, Earth visibility, communication availability, potential solar energy generation, landing location, mission date and time, data accuracy, and system reliability.

We also prioritized accessibility through a fully Arabic, right-to-left interface, a simple user experience, and optional AI functionality that does not affect the core scientific calculations.
